entities.summary:
Caius Poetelius Libo Visolus (b. 400 BCE, Rome) was a Roman Senator and military commander active in the late 4th century BCE. He played a key role in the transformation of the Roman Republic into the Roman Empire under the leadership of the Julian clan. The Poetelii family was a prominent patrician family in Rome, known for their distinguished service to the Roman state. Poetelius Libo Visolus was the father of Caius Poetelius Magnus, who would later become a prominent Roman Senator and military commander in his own right. The Poetelii family was known for their wealth, influence, and political power, which they wielded through a network of alliances and strategic marriages. Poetelius Libo Visolus's military campaigns were marked by their brutality and efficiency, earning him a reputation as a skilled and ruthless commander. He was known for his ability to adapt to changing circumstances on the battlefield, often using innovative tactics to outmaneuver his opponents. The impact of Poetelius Libo Visolus's military campaigns can still be felt today, as they helped to establish the Roman Empire's dominance over the Mediterranean region. His legacy also lived on through his family, who continued to play important roles in Roman politics and society for generations to come.

The Poetelii family's influence extended far beyond Rome, as they were also patrons of the arts and literature. Poetelius Libo Visolus was known for his patronage of the poet Ennius, who would go on to become one of the most celebrated Roman poets of all time. The Poetelii family's love of literature and the arts was a hallmark of their distinguished reputation, and they continued to support the arts throughout their history.
